SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: He reports onset of low back pain on 06/06/2026. He describes mechanical low back pain radiating to the left buttock, worsened by prolonged sitting and flexion. He denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bowel or bladder incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
Exam: Lumbar spine inspection normal, palpation reveals paraspinal tenderness left L4-L5. Straight leg raise positive at 40 degrees left. Exam shows diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness consistent with radiculopathy. Strength 5/0 elsewhere.
Assessment: Acute lumbar radiculopathy, likely L5/S1, M54.16.
Plan: Start NSAIDs today (06/07/2026). Initiate physical therapy starting 06/11/2026 for core strengthening and lumbar stabilization. Continue activity as tolerated. Follow up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient returns for follow-up after completing prescribed NSAIDs and physical therapy. He reports ongoing low back pain with left leg radiculopathy, unchanged since last visit.
Exam: Similar to prior, with persistent diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy with partial response to NSAIDs and no improvement after physical therapy.
Plan: He was prescribed NSAIDs from 06/07/2026 to 07/16/2026, which provided partial relief. He completed a course of physical therapy from 06/11/2026 to 07/16/2026 for 10 sessions without improvement. Obtain lumbar MRI to further evaluate; consider spine surgery referral pending results.

Plan: He was prescribed NSAIDs from 06/07/2026 to 07/16/2026, which provided partial relief. He completed a course of physical therapy from 06/11/2026 to 07/16/2026 for 10 sessions without improvement. Lumbar MRI will be ordered to further evaluate. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings.

HPI: Patient returns after decision to obtain lumbar MRI based on persistent radiculopathy lacking improvement with NSAIDs and physical therapy.

Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today (07/31/2026). Results will guide further management, including possible spine surgery referral.
